examples.8.1 Why game design needs diagrams: Moonshift carried two game-flow diagrams for three weeks; the newer one still sent Pause to the title screen, so QA tested the wrong exit. We deleted the stale export, dated the source, and made Pause return to the live shift, which turned the diagram into one answer: where does Pause return?
examples.8.2 The translation table: For Moonshift the translation table maps use case to the mode map, activity to Nia's garden quest, state machine to B.E.E.P.'s repair states, sequence to the 100 ms repair confirmation, class to the save entities, component to the air/power systems map, ERD to inventory, and BPMN to the air economy. The table settled that the slice needs eight diagrams, not a full UML set.
examples.8.3 Diagram standards: Moonshift uses one legend: rounded rectangles for modes, rectangles for systems, diamonds for decisions, blue for player actions, orange for base systems, and red for air loss; every diagram carries an owner, date, and version. The standard settled that the old red/green air gauge failed colour-blind testers, so we added a shape-coded warning icon.
examples.8.4 Game flow / mode map: Moonshift's mode map has Title, Save Select, Gameplay HUD, Pause, Map, Quest Log, Results, and Settings, with one clear exit per screen and a dashed autosave transition at shift end. It settled that Pause must freeze the air timer and return to the live shift, not the title, which removed a QA blocker.
examples.8.5 Core loop (nested loops): Moonshift's core loop has three nested frames: the 30-second scan → choose → place → watch exchange, the 8-minute shift of route → repair → ration, and the 12-shift campaign of upgrade → specialise → replay. The diagram settled that the gauge must move within 200 ms of placement, so we cut the 1.2-second repair animation.
examples.8.6 State machine (player, AI, session): Moonshift's repair-bot state machine has Idle, Scan, Place, Repair, Reroute, Overclock, and Depleted, with transitions such as scan → target found, repair → parts missing, and overclock → power below 2. It settled that Overclock interrupts Repair and falls to Depleted on timeout, which fixed the shift-5 soft lock.
examples.8.7 Activity / quest flowchart: Moonshift's garden quest for Nia is a flowchart: Talk to Nia → Trace the frozen pipe → Thaw the line → Repair the cut → Restart the pump, with a diamond for the hidden cut and a recoverable fail if the garden dries. It settled that the quest can finish without the optional seed cache, so that branch stays side content.
examples.8.8 Sequence / interaction timing: Moonshift's repair sequence diagram runs Player → Input → Gameplay → UI → Audio: tap, validate placement, update air, play the hiss, show the gauge, inside a 16 ms input poll and an 80 ms tap-to-feedback budget. It settled that the air gauge updates before the repair animation, so the result is visible even when the animation is skipped.
examples.8.9 Systems map / dependency graph: Moonshift's systems map has Air, Power, Cargo, Crew, Rooms, Save, and HUD, with Power → Air for fans, Cargo → Air for filters, Crew → Air for upkeep, and Save reading all persistent state. It settled that Crew owns trust and Gameplay owns air, ending the duplicate write that desynced shift summaries.
examples.8.10 Class / entity data model: Moonshift's entity model has Outpost, Room, AirNetwork, Inventory, CrewMember, and ShiftState; Room owns 1..n Vents, Inventory holds 0..n PartStacks, and ShiftState references the active Room and crew. It settled that PartDef holds item stats while PartStack stores only defId and quantity, so save migration never duplicates stats.
examples.8.11 Economy flow (faucets, sinks, pools: Moonshift's air economy flow runs from Processing and Tanks (+18 air per shift) into the Air pool (cap 100), then out to crew upkeep (−8) and leaks (−4 to −12), with a converter turning 2 Parts into 1 Filter. It settled that shift 4 ran a 33% surplus at the low leak rate, so we lowered tank output instead of adding a sink.
examples.8.12 Level flow / beat chart (map + paci: Moonshift's level flow and beat chart run Arrival → First Breath → First Shortage → First Setback → Final Shift, with the 3×3 board, two-room split, leak-and-timer, and whole-base reroute as beats; the intensity curve peaks at the whole-base reroute. It settled that the first real failure belongs after two successes, so the leak moved to shift 3.
examples.8.13 Narrative branch graph: Moonshift's narrative branch graph runs Arrival → Radio Call or Workshop Salvage, then three endings: Rescue (radio repaired, crew trust 50+), Holdout (air stable, garden alive), and Departure (lander repaired, trust under 25). It settled that the garden choice must set world_garden_alive at the climax, so the epilogue varies without a fourth ending.
examples.8.14 Progression / unlock graph: Moonshift's unlock graph runs Place → Dismantle → Reroute → Overclock → Room Chain, with each node opening a room or verb and no node having more than two parents; the optional challenge room sits off Reroute. It settled that Overclock arrives at shift 5, after the player has felt a power shortage.
examples.8.15 UX screen flow and wireframe: Moonshift's screen flow has Title → Save Select → HUD ⇄ Pause, with Map, Quest Log, Settings, and Results as one-input branches; the HUD wireframe puts air and power top-left, the shift timer top-centre, objectives right, and the interact prompt near the reticle. It settled that Pause must freeze the timer and keep the live frame visible.
examples.8.16 Which diagram goes in which GDD tab: Moonshift assigns the mode map and core loop to 02 Gameplay & Systems, the garden quest and branch graph to 03 Narrative & World, the entity model and save ERD to 06 Technical Design, and the HUD flow to 04 Experience. The matrix settled that the air economy belongs in 02, not 07 Production, and that the producer owns the roadmap update.
examples.8.17 Tooling: Moonshift uses FigJam for the mode map and HUD flow, draw.io for the entity model and save ERD, Machinations for the air economy, Twine for the garden and ending branches, and a spreadsheet for every air and power number. The stack settled that the team reviews one FigJam board on Fridays and exports PNGs into the GDD.
examples.8.18 Review checklist: Before the Moonshift vertical-slice review, the mode map passed all ten checks, including one question, a legend, labelled arrows, failure and pause exits, a dated source link, and alt text naming the three ways a shift ends. The review caught that Results had no back edge, which we fixed before QA.
